description: database-slices differential chain (work unit 4.380) over the EPLDatabaseTimeBatch execution (ordinal 5) of regression-lib/src/main/java/com/espertech/esper/regressionlib/suite/epl/database/EPLDatabaseJoin.java — the first of the three time-batch variants; the sibling EPLDatabaseTimeBatchOM (java-runtime-b86f31a8dc33eda9fc51) and EPLDatabaseTimeBatchCompile (java-runtime-d1a52864d392f7c194e5) executions replay the identical shared runtestTimeBatch runner over a SODA object model and an eplToModel round-trip respectively and stay implemented-not-differential pending the Go compile surface, and this slice opens the time-batch differential that draft 4.379 deferred for engine-level investigation of the window-release/poll interaction. The Java oracle runs against the established esper-mysql mysql:8.0 Docker fixture (docker run --name esper-mysql -e MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=password -e MYSQL_DATABASE=test -p 3306:3306 -d mysql:8.0, readiness via mysqladmin ping, fixture loaded from common/etc/regression/create_testdb.sql with the '//'-comment lines stripped; the load tolerates the pre-existing mytesttable_large/mytestupsert re-create errors so it is idempotent) and connects through SupportDatabaseService constants: DRIVER com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver, FULLURL jdbc:mysql://localhost/test?user=root&password=password&useSSL=false. Session configuration mirrors TestSuiteEPLDatabase.configure restricted to this execution: the SupportBean POJO event type (the only event type it names) and the 'MyDBWithRetain' database reference configured as a DriverManagerConnection (DRIVER/FULLURL/SupportDatabaseURL.newProperties()) with ConnectionLifecycleEnum RETAIN and no cache; the suite's setEnableJDBC(true)/setEnableQueryPlan(true) logging flags are dropped because they alter log observability only and have no recorded effect. Internal timer off, epoch initialization 0, per-case fresh runtime (undeployAll after the case body, destroy in finally, runtime URI derived from the pinned java-runtime id). Byte-exact statement (assembled with the suite's own ALL_FIELDS concatenation, exact spacing preserved): timebatch (ordinal 5) deploys '@name('s0') select mybigint, myint, myvarchar, mychar, mybool, mynumeric, mydecimal, mydouble, myreal from  sql:MyDBWithRetain ['select mybigint, myint, myvarchar, mychar, mybool, mynumeric, mydecimal, mydouble, myreal from mytesttable \n\r where ${intPrimitive} = mytesttable.mybigint'] as s0,SupportBean#time_batch(10 sec) as s1' — DOUBLE space after 'from' (the select segment ends 'from ' and the historical segment starts ' sql:'), a literal LF+CR escape pair ('\n\r', carriage return AFTER newline) between 'mytesttable ' and 'where' inside the SQL, and NO space after 'as s0,' before the SupportBean segment ('as s0,SupportBean#time_batch(10 sec) as s1'); advance-time semantics are env.advanceTime -> runtime.getEventService().advanceTime per RegressionEnvironmentBase. Replay of the shared runtestTimeBatch runner: env.advanceTime(0) after the deploy, then the iterator over myint asserted EMPTY in-process (no record); send SupportBean(intPrimitive=10) — the historical poll fires at send time and the joined mybigint-10 row (myint 100) is ITERATOR-VISIBLE immediately while the triggering event sits in the time_batch window, asserted in-process ordered compare [100] and recorded as count iterator-rows=1; send SB(5) — iterator [100,50] in-process, count iterator-rows=2; the suite's milestone(0) replayed as the documented no-op it is in RegressionEnvironmentBase; send SB(2) — iterator [100,50,20] in-process, count iterator-rows=3; advanceTime(10000) — TimeBatchView.sendBatch releases the batch of three trigger events into the join and the flush delivers exactly the three joined rows [myint 100,50,20] to the listener as ONE new-data delivery recorded as the listener record (the first release posts a NULL old-data array because TimeBatchView indicates the prior batch as old data and lastBatch is still empty — asserted in-process; no further release happens because the internal timer is off and time never advances again); each flushed row is asserted in full in-process against the seed values with BigDecimal equals: row mybigint 10 = {10,100,'J','P',true,NULL,1000,10.2,10.3} (the NULL mynumeric stays Java-null in-process), row mybigint 5 = {5,50,'E','V',false,500,500,5.2,5.3}, row mybigint 2 = {2,20,'B','Y',false,100,200,2.2,2.3}; then the iterator is asserted EMPTY in-process because the released window cleared, recorded as count iterator-rows=0; send SB(9) — the poll re-fires and the joined mybigint-9 row is iterator-visible while batched, iterator [90] in-process, count iterator-rows=1; send SB(8) — iterator [90,80] in-process, count iterator-rows=2 (both sends stay batched; the listener stays silent). Record protocol: one record per listener delivery {case, operation:'listener', statement:'s0', sequence, time, new:[rows]} where rows are projected {kind:'row', fields:{...}} objects under the canonical output names mybigint/myint/myvarchar/mychar/mybool/mynumeric/mydecimal/mydouble/myreal with field names sorted alphabetically for human-diffable traces (the canonical comparator is order-insensitive). Value forms, both sides matching because the Go side feeds the identical canonical 10-row fixture through a function-fed HistoricalProvider (no database driver): mybigint as JSON number (int64), myint as JSON number, myvarchar/mychar as JSON strings (MySQL strips CHAR(20) trailing spaces; the flushed myvarchar values are 'J','E','B' and mychar 'P','V','Y'), mybool as JSON true/false (true,false,false for rows 10/5/2), mynumeric/mydecimal as JSON STRINGS of the scale-0 BigDecimal (asserted scale 0 in-process; '1000' for row 10's mydecimal, '500','500' for row 5, '100','200' for row 2), mydouble/myreal as JSON numbers (10.2/5.2/2.2 and 10.3/5.3/2.3), and NULL column values as the differential protocol null marker object {'state':'null'} — the canonical null form both the committed Java oracle convention and the Go NormalizeResults renderer emit, so bare JSON null is never emitted because the Go side cannot produce it; the NULL mynumeric columns belong to seed rows 7-10 and row mybigint 10 is among the flushed rows, so the listener record carries exactly ONE null marker (row 10's mynumeric) while rows 5 and 2 carry the non-null scale-0 strings. Count records are {case, operation:'count', statement:'flow', sequence, time, name, count} mirroring the dataflow-oracle convention the Go runner pairs with (iterator-rows); count records are emitted at the same positions as the corresponding in-process iterator compares, so the case's record order is count iterator-rows=1, count iterator-rows=2, count iterator-rows=3, listener flush of 3 rows, count iterator-rows=0, count iterator-rows=1, count iterator-rows=2. Sequence is case-local restarting at 1, the time is the fixed epoch 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. The 7 records (6 counts + 1 listener delivery of 3 rows) carry the database-timebatch differential chain for the Go case builder.
